skill.name: resend-api
skill.description: Use when sending transactional or batch emails from Node.js with Resend — including React email templates, attachments, and audiences.
whenToUse: Sending transactional emails (receipts, password resets, notifications) from a backend
Rendering email templates with React via react-email
Sending batch emails or managing contacts and audiences
Verifying sending domains and handling email webhooks

keyConcepts.explanation: Instantiated with `new Resend(apiKey)`. All operations hang off this client: resend.emails, resend.batch, resend.domains, resend.audiences, resend.contacts.
The `from` address must use a domain you've verified in Resend (DKIM/SPF). Unverified domains can only send from the onboarding@resend.dev test sender.
Pass a React component to the `react` field; Resend renders it to HTML server-side. Works with the react-email component library.
resend.batch.send() accepts an array of up to 100 email objects in one call, each delivered independently.
Pass an idempotencyKey in the request options to prevent duplicate sends on retries within the idempotency window.
Resend posts events (email.sent, email.delivered, email.bounced, email.complained, email.opened, email.clicked) signed via Svix headers for verification.

apiReference.purpose: Create the Resend SDK client with your API key.
apiReference.example:
import { Resend } from 'resend';
const resend = new Resend(process.env.RESEND_API_KEY);

apiReference.signature: resend.emails.send({ from, to, subject, html | text | react, ... })
apiReference.purpose: Send a single email; returns { data: { id }, error }.
Render a React component to HTML for the email body.

apiReference.signature: send with cc, bcc, reply_to, attachments, headers, tags
apiReference.purpose: Add CC/BCC recipients, reply-to, file attachments, custom headers, and metadata tags.
Send up to 100 emails in a single request.
Pass options to make a send idempotent across retries.
Manage sending domains, marketing audiences, and their contacts via the SDK.
apiReference.example:
await resend.domains.create({ name: 'acme.com' });
await resend.contacts.create({ email: 'user@e.com', audienceId: 'aud_123' });

apiReference.purpose: Retrieve a sent email's status, update a scheduled email, or cancel a scheduled send.
apiReference.example:
const { data } = await resend.emails.get('email_id');
await resend.emails.cancel('email_id');

gotchas: The `from` domain must be verified in Resend; otherwise sends fail unless you use onboarding@resend.dev for testing.
The SDK does not throw on API errors — always check the returned `error` field alongside `data`.
Free/test API keys can only send to your own verified email address until a domain is verified.
Batch send is capped at 100 emails per request, and batch does not support attachments or scheduled_at.
Verify webhooks using the Svix signature headers (svix-id, svix-timestamp, svix-signature); don't trust unsigned payloads.
Attachment content should be a Buffer or base64 string; very large attachments hit per-message size limits.
Scheduling uses scheduled_at with an ISO 8601 or natural-language time; past times send immediately.
Rate limits apply per account (default ~2 requests/sec); handle 429 responses with backoff.
